@graph.name: Undisclosed implementation choices (19:40 to 20:41)
@graph.description: Manu Seyfzadeh. He filled gaps experimentally for sub-aperture synthesis, registration and depth focusing. He describes his own implementation. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

@graph.name: Fixed half-band reference (Human prompt following the band-pass filter design question)
@graph.description: Manu Seyfzadeh. He proposes a fixed half-band master and many partly overlapping half-band copies. English. Written prompt by Seyfzadeh; his technical interpretation, no Biondi confirmation.

@graph.name: Suggested 1-100 Hz range (Human question about whether seismic frequencies between 1 and 100 Hz are plausible)
@graph.description: Manu Seyfzadeh. He asks if 1-100 Hz could be the band for seismic frequencies. ChatGPT agrees. English. Written question by Seyfzadeh; model answer excluded.

@graph.name: Interpreting a surface ellipse (20:20 to 22:18)
@graph.description: Manu Seyfzadeh. He describes a surface ellipse from vertical and transverse oscillation as his interpretation, drawing on an external geophysicist. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

@graph.name: Pairing two displaced looks (29:50 to 31:07)
@graph.description: Manu Seyfzadeh. He uses a single flyover, many Doppler sub-apertures, and slightly displaced reference and offset copies within each one. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

@graph.name: Focusing against candidate depths (35:19 to 36:02)
@graph.description: Manu Seyfzadeh. He describes an adjoint focusing operator against theoretical phase histories for candidate depths. Biondi asks about the displacement matrix. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

@graph.name: Encoding vibration direction (44:05 to 45:32)
@graph.description: Filippo Biondi. He proposes extending the display to encode horizontal, vertical and oblique vibration orientation using a second polarimetry patent. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

@graph.name: Choosing the section direction (55:24 to 56:28)
@graph.description: Filippo Biondi. Biondi recommends a range-oriented section. He describes lower quality when the line and sub-aperture split are both in azimuth. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

@graph.name: Coarse and fine registration windows (56:37 to 57:11)
@graph.description: Manu Seyfzadeh. His coarse registration frame is 128 by 128 pixels. The fine frame is 24 azimuth by 32 range pixels. He tested recovery with injected vectors. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

@graph.name: Converting pixel shifts to metres (53:52 to 54:31)
@graph.description: Manu Seyfzadeh. He converts range and azimuth pixel scales independently to metres from delivered metadata. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

@graph.name: Calibrating the rock-speed model (47:36 to 48:34)
@graph.description: Manu Seyfzadeh. He says he changed the rock-speed model, calibrated with Campbell’s Tomb and a shaft by Khufu, then applied the derived rule to Osiris. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

@graph.name: Choosing the wavelength (1:21:43 to 1:21:59)
@graph.description: Manu Seyfzadeh. He says he used a different wavelength from 0.24 m and again cites calibration at Campbell’s Tomb. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

@graph.name: Uncertainty in the depth estimate (1:21:22 to 1:21:37)
@graph.description: Filippo Biondi. Reviewing the Khafre similarity, Biondi says the depth estimate still needs work. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

@graph.name: Changing the sub-aperture count (1:23:34 to 1:24:00)
@graph.description: Seyfzadeh, then Biondi. Seyfzadeh says K was 295. Biondi suggests trying 5000 after seeing the output. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

@graph.name: Version and filter changes (1:26:56 to 1:27:39)
@graph.description: Trevor Grassi. He distinguishes a first Osiris output, a 100 m version described as 3360 pixels, and a later version with stronger filtering. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

@graph.name: Aligning output with a drawing (1:28:02 to 1:29:00)
@graph.description: Trevor Grassi. He marked corresponding spots in Photoshop and discusses matching a perspective drawing to a different section view. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

@graph.name: First tests with a Capella image (37:30 to 38:00)
@graph.description: Manu Seyfzadeh. Initial Giza tests used a lower-resolution image supplied without charge by Capella. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

@graph.name: Sharing an image and a line (51:34 to 51:56)
@graph.description: Manu Seyfzadeh. He says a placement line was sent to Biondi and both had access to the image from Athanatos. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

@graph.name: Confidence in the Osiris identification (43:48 to 44:04)
@graph.description: Manu Seyfzadeh. His expressed confidence in seeing Osiris is above 50 percent and below 100 percent at this point. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

@graph.name: Horizontal mismatch in the Khufu overlay (1:45:48 to 1:46:30)
@graph.description: Trevor Grassi. In his Khufu overlay, Grassi asks viewers to compare chamber heights and notes the horizontal mismatch. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

@graph.name: Doppler bandwidth and half-band scanning (25:12 to 26:20)
@graph.description: Filippo Biondi. He describes spotlight Doppler bandwidths of roughly 22-25 kHz and using half the available band to scan along the aperture. He separately mentions a roughly 10 GHz carrier. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

@graph.name: Moving processing to GPUs (26:40 to 27:11)
@graph.description: Filippo Biondi. Biondi says they optimized the kernel and were moving towards GPU processing while retaining the same technique. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

@graph.name: Retuning the method for depth (29:54 to 30:50)
@graph.description: Filippo Biondi. He says they tuned the software differently once the aim changed from the top of the pyramid to deeper targets. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

@graph.name: Averaging several Gran Sasso sections (2:54:27 to 2:57:37)
@graph.description: Filippo Biondi. For the wide Gran Sasso target he describes wider focusing and averaging several lines pixel by pixel to reduce noise. He reports at least two months of processing. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

@graph.name: Discarding noise-dominated outputs (20:50 to 21:30)
@graph.description: Filippo Biondi. He says they discarded many trials where noise was inverted and kept successes. He mentions hundreds of successes on other things. Italian. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

@graph.name: MATLAB to CUDA processing times (2:20:00 to 2:21:14)
@graph.description: Filippo Biondi. He describes the Gran Sasso demonstration as software 1.0, a MATLAB to C++/CUDA rewrite, and a change from about a month to three or four hours. Italian. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

@graph.name: Coherent processing of complex returns (23:35 to 24:45)
@graph.description: Filippo Biondi. He says the processing is coherent and handles real and imaginary components. It uses an aperture of displaced measurements to infer direction. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

@graph.name: A three-band colour image (33:05 to 33:38)
@graph.description: Filippo Biondi. He describes a colour Capella image made from three Doppler bands. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

@graph.name: Pseudo-inversion and the role of AI (55:18 to 57:10)
@graph.description: Filippo Biondi. He says the model is pseudo-inverted, reports four providers and distinguishes that reconstruction from AI. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

@graph.name: Limits of spiral interpretation (47:17 to 50:09)
@graph.description: Filippo Biondi. He describes the spiral as a shape. He cannot distinguish stairs from cables and describes material recognition as future work requiring ground truth. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

@graph.name: Depth depends on the local geology (Podcast 23:30 (publisher segment timestamp))
@graph.description: Filippo Biondi. He says accurate depth needs the local geological model and constant density produces only a rough estimate. English. Creator-supplied RSS transcript, paraphrased.

@graph.name: Unscaled depth axis in the spiral model (Podcast 26:15 (publisher segment timestamp))
@graph.description: Filippo Biondi. Biondi says the displayed spiral model has an unscaled depth axis. He says in-person examination would distinguish what the apparent spiral represents. English. Creator-supplied RSS transcript, paraphrased.

@graph.description: Khafre Project speaker at Bologna (Italian release). The presentation explicitly counts pixels relative to the 137 m height of Khafre and reads 648 m to the end platform. The speaker acknowledges obliquity and argues that the angular errors cancel in the ratio. Italian. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

@graph.description: Mixed panel; speaker changes in captions. The panel discusses a visible cutoff near 550-600 m and questions a deeper estimate. Attribution changes during the exchange. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

@graph.name: Claim to have measured the Big Void (1:02:15 to 1:03:00)
@graph.description: Filippo Biondi. He says their model contains the Big Void and they measured its dimensions. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

@graph.name: Separating Big Void and corridor priority (1:40:37 to 1:41:50)
@graph.description: Filippo Biondi. The conversation identifies Big Void on a slide. Biondi associates his six-month priority claim with the corridor in the following sentences. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

@graph.name: Claimed orientation of the Big Void (5:19 to 6:00)
@graph.description: Filippo Biondi. He tells Matt Beall that they detected the Big Void and offers a different orientation from the Grand Gallery. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

@graph.name: Selecting the second-Sphinx search area (15:12 to 16:33)
@graph.description: Filippo Biondi. He describes selecting the second Sphinx location after Damiano Piras and others suggested that area. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

@graph.name: Compute requirements in meeting footage (11:40 to 13:50)
@graph.description: Filippo Biondi. In edited meeting footage, he describes using multiple cores and needing more computing capacity. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

@graph.name: An unspecified stage in the 2022 paper (50:05 to 51:39)
@graph.description: Manu Seyfzadeh. In his 2022 reading of the paper, he notes that he could not find a detailed explanation of one stage. This predates his later reconstruction. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

@graph.name: Carlin Tunnel as a proposed example (Post text, Carlin Tunnel railway, Nevada)
@graph.description: Filippo Biondi. He describes deep geocoding with one SLC and names the Carlin railway tunnel as an example. English. Author-written public post; paraphrased.

@graph.name: Program claims and intended external review (Initial report, abstract and project introduction)
@graph.description: Grassi and Frank Rogala. The program attributes deep imaging and material identification to the software and describes a proposed third-party check under NDA. English. Written program statement; paraphrased.

@graph.name: Eight shafts and two large chambers (Conference abstract, Second Step, March 16 2025)
@graph.description: Khafre Project (three signatories). The signed abstract describes eight shafts, two rows, 648 m depth and two cubes of approximately 80 m per side. It credits Capella and Umbra and multiple tomograms. English. Signed author abstract; paraphrased.

@graph.name: Tracking the Doppler centroid (1:12:18 to 1:13:09)
@graph.description: Filippo Biondi. He says changing surface motion shifts the estimated Doppler centroid. He records its history and attempts the inversion from it. Italian. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

@graph.name: Vegetation as a source of noise (1:13:10 to 1:14:10)
@graph.description: Filippo Biondi. Biondi expects dense vegetation to add noise and says he has not tested strongly vegetated terrain. Italian. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

@graph.description: Filippo Biondi. He says air inside a chamber should appear dark and its borders bright in his tomogram. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

@graph.description: Filippo Biondi. He says to select two image pixels, draw a line and extract a vertical section. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

@graph.name: Repeated Fourier transforms and runtime (40:01 to 41:04)
@graph.description: Filippo Biondi. He describes calculating shifts with repeated FFTs and inverse FFTs over a large data region. He gives roughly two weeks of continuous processing for the example. English. Public captions with timecodes; paraphrased.

@graph.description: Independent controls-first tracker and depth-operator analysis. Executed the deterministic expected-power routine and checked its answer using independent QR and impulse propagation. Its null applies to accumulated and detrended noise.

@graph.description: Independent CUDA chain and observation-space benchmark. Optional one-sided filtering encodes a sign convention. Blind recovery of physical polarity would need signed ground truth. The benchmark supplies its own forward-model observations.

@graph.name: simossss/sar-tomography-reproduction
@graph.description: Independent Umbra single-pass surrogate plus separate Sentinel-1 multi-pass test. The single-pass branch averages reconstructed complex values per subband. Its scores test a different observable from paired displacement.

@graph.name: emmanuel6474/biondirepro
@graph.description: Independent Vesuvius operator and published-figure audit. Useful control designs and source-fidelity checks. This is not Biondi’s processing source or a sensor-to-cavity validation.

@graph.name: juanvillaverde/harmonicsar
@graph.description: Public HarmonicSAR marketing site. The only JavaScript file in this revision runs the web interface and canvas illustration.

@graph.name: Identify the observation
@graph.text: Six public complex images include amplitude, phase and acquisition geometry.
@graph.description: The exact acquisition and pre-color numerical section behind the 648 m drawing remain unknown.

@graph.name: Split the aperture
@graph.text: Biondi describes using half the Doppler band. Seyfzadeh also describes a fixed master.
@graph.description: Original mask edges, time mapping and pair spacing for each published section remain unspecified.

@graph.name: Track apparent shifts
@graph.text: Seyfzadeh describes coarse 128 × 128 sampling followed by 24 azimuth × 32 range samples.
@graph.description: Product spacing changes the physical footprint. Fine image shifts lack a colocated ground-motion record at Giza.

@graph.name: Set the height scale
@graph.text: Equations 20-24 link paired image offsets to complex steering vectors under an assumed wavelength.
@graph.description: The baseline convention, extra phase factor, seismic wavelength and subsurface transfer are not calibrated for these scenes.

@graph.name: Focus the signal
@graph.text: The paper describes a Fourier-like inverse. Seyfzadeh says he used an adjoint.
@graph.description: The exact regularization and numerical scores before filtering the published authors' images are missing.

@graph.name: Test position and shape
@graph.text: The surveyed plan and approximate signed floor heights supply independent comparison coordinates.
@graph.description: A high value at one supplied height does not identify the walls or free height maximum.

@graph.name: Test outside the training case
@graph.text: Separate acquisitions, a driven reflector and two independently surveyed underground directions provide distinct tests.
@graph.description: The checked archives contain no unused surveyed target with all inputs for blind shaft depth validation.

@graph.name: One fixed room position across six scenes

@graph.text: A rule chosen at the supplied King's floor should rank the same location highly on other passes.

@graph.description: At +43 m the King's location beat 31, 32 and 31 of 32 neighbors on the long passes, then 26, 17 and 21 on Umbra. Only October beat all 32.

@graph.text: The locked rule passed two of five transfer scenes at King's. No scene passed for all three chambers.
@graph.nextTest: Forecast an unseen surveyed location before seeing any labels.

@graph.text: If the signal measures the King's floor, let the peak select its own height.

@graph.description: Over -44 to +44 m the King's peaks were +1, +1, -1.5, -29, -0.5 and -5.5 m. The supplied floor was +43 m.

@graph.text: None recovered the floor. A location comparison at a supplied height and an unrestricted height estimate answer different questions.
@graph.nextTest: Predict two unseen depth marks with a fixed vertical scale and benchmark.

@graph.text: Biondi describes a dark room interior bounded by bright edges.

@graph.description: At the King's room, wall-minus-center was negative on all three passes. Ranks were 1, 0 and 1 of 32. Queen ranks were 3, 23 and 27. Zero of six met the signed, rotated and baseline gates.

@graph.text: This planned-outline approximation failed. The author's original vertical cross-section was unavailable for direct comparison.
@graph.nextTest: Compare walls in the native numerical section against a registered independent survey.

@graph.text: Could a nearby location achieve two transfers with the same training freedom?

@graph.description: Each of the 32 shifted King locations tried the same 36 recipes. Zero passed on both later long scenes. The survey position passed both. None of 12 randomized-phase images passed there.

@graph.text: The contrast depends on complex image structure. Surface scattering could produce such structure. The positions overlap.
@graph.nextTest: Repeat on independent sites with surveyed positives and negatives.

@graph.text: Two Capella views might select surface details that persist better than one view.

@graph.description: Two-view picks matched ICEYE and at least one Umbra image within 8 m in 16/162 blocks. Single-view prominence and brightness gave 14/162 and 10/162.

@graph.text: Some surface features repeated. The paired comparison did not establish an advantage over either single-view baseline.
@graph.nextTest: Evaluate the fixed selector in another landscape. This endpoint measures the surface.

@graph.text: Raw pulse phase should supply a stable Khafre motion series before assigning depth.

@graph.description: Zero of eight Capella blocks passed the target phase gate. Zero of four short Umbra blocks passed. All 12 injected moving-point controls passed.

@graph.text: Natural motion remained unresolved at Khafre in these blocks. Complete Capella phase-history files were verified; these fits used declared pulse subsets.
@graph.nextTest: Measure a surveyed stable target and synchronize a surface-motion sensor during the pass.

@graph.text: A radar spectral centroid should recover motion of an instrumented driven reflector.

@graph.description: The primary seven-sample window gave 2.01 Hz for a 2 Hz drive and beat eight comparison locations. Ideal-response correction gave 5.98 mm/s RMS versus the 6.66 mm/s ground reference.

@graph.text: A driven surface reflector supplies a positive motion check. No underground target was involved.
@graph.nextTest: Run the same estimator against independently instrumented weaker targets.

@graph.text: Radar imagery might predict known underground axes before the survey labels are opened.

@graph.description: El Osario cave missed its surveyed axis by 61.72°. Teotihuacan tunnel missed by 88°. Both exceeded the fixed 15° tolerance. Simple brightness missed by 35.84° and 89°.

@graph.text: Both orientation tests failed. Locations and monument names were known. El Osario used complex ICEYE, Teotihuacan a processed Umbra image.
@graph.nextTest: Use the same complex-image estimator at a new site and seal the survey before analysis.

@graph.text: Can a harmonic-window setting selected on the October King's position transfer to September?

@graph.description: The October P2/W25 winner beat 24/24 neighbors in training and 13/24 in September. This was a different 300-setting search, with different sites and controls.

@graph.text: The tuned October result failed to transfer at its original gate. Keep it distinct from the September-trained 36-recipe test.
@graph.nextTest: Compare algorithms on one common predeclared unseen target.

@graph.text: Can the previously fixed harmonic score separate each room from every translation on X50?

@graph.description: King, Queen and Subterranean beat 0, 27 and 9 of 32 positions. The exterior square beat 47/48.

@graph.text: The three chamber locations missed that protocol's strict 32/32 gate. Its harmonic statistic differs from the new weighted complex filter.
@graph.nextTest: Compare scores on further acquisitions under one fixed set of labels.

@graph.text: A frozen depth-to-wavelength ratio should explain the second date better than ordinary smooth drift.

@graph.description: The chosen oscillator reduced October residual power by 47.91%. A quadratic trend with the same count of fitted coefficients reduced it by 63.23%. Both compare with linear drift.

@graph.text: Smooth drift explains more of this observed trace. This single-component test used 24 neighbors and allowed a new complex amplitude per date.
@graph.nextTest: Predict a calibrated response without fitting a separate excitation for each observation.

@graph.text: Biondi says averaging adjacent lines reduces noise. Does that improve the repeated fit?

@graph.description: One, three and five parallel-line choices produced no two-date chamber pass at the preset rule. On published cemetery lines, only one of three withheld lines had a nonzero value at the selected cell.

@graph.text: These two tests apply to different inputs. The cemetery values are already filtered output, with a supplied relative coordinate system.
@graph.nextTest: Request original unfiltered parallel lines with their physical spacing, direction and selection rule.

@graph.name: Can the traces select deep over shallow?

@graph.text: The same hundred tracked observations might distinguish shallow from deep support.

@graph.description: At 0.24 m wavelength, both a 0-200 m model and a disjoint 520-800 m model fit to relative residual below 5 × 10⁻¹⁴. Fitting either profile on one date predicted the other worse than zero.

@graph.text: The unrestricted complex profile is underdetermined in this model. A constrained, independently calibrated physical model may behave differently.
@graph.nextTest: Use independently measured wave speed, mode and phase, then predict a depth withheld from fitting.

@graph.name: Can measured gravity resolve the 648 m bracket?

@graph.text: The proposed missing rock should have a gravity signature measurable near Khafre.

@graph.description: The nearest of 71 checked Egyptian gravity records was 5.83 km away. The benchmark shaft model predicts 0.044 µGal there, versus a 10 µGal reporting increment.

@graph.text: This published sample cannot determine the shaft bottoms. The signed 648 m label is a published drawing dimension.
@graph.nextTest: Test a surveyed vertical return with an identifiable endpoint and an independent velocity measurement.
